newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila may seek FBI help in probe on Moslem deaths.
newsitem.headline: Manila may seek FBI help in probe on Moslem deaths.

text.p: The Philippines said on Tuesday it may ask the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to determine who fired shells that killed 11 civilians during fighting between soldiers and Moslem rebels.

Commissioner Nasser Marohomsalic of the state's Human Rights Commission said relatives of 10 Moslem students and their teacher, killed when mortar shells hit an Islamic school on March 16, had agreed in principle to exhume the victims' bodies.
The relatives have asked the commission to subject the metal fragments recovered from the scene of the shelling to ballistic tests by an independent agency, Marohomsalic told reporters.
"Since the commission has no laboratory for the purpose, it will ask the University of the Philippines to do it or the Federal Bureau of Investigation of the United States," he said.
Commission officials said they would consider seeking FBI help because of the bureau's expertise, which may not be available from local independent agencies.
Scientists from the state-run university have in the past been involved in the investigation of violent deaths.
The defence department has said it is setting up a special panel to investigate the incident.
Guerrillas of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) have accused the army of shelling the school house during a mortar exchange in Buldon town in Maguindanao province.
The military has denied the accusation, saying the school was beyond the range of its cannons.
The incident coincided with exploratory peace talks between Manila and the MILF, a breakaway Moslem faction which is fighting for an Islamic state in the southern islands.
The MILF is not part of a peace deal concluded by Manila last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front.

Marohomsalic said that while relatives had agreed in principle to exhuming the victims' bodies, they suggested that Islamic religious leaders should first be consulted to determine the appropriateness in unearthing the bodies.
